diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The task failed on Step 2 (gold valuation exposure) and Step 3 (RaR percentage). The agent's Step 2 risk values are ~sqrt(3) times larger than expected (e.g., Belarus 1024.59 vs expected ~592.5), indicating the agent incorrectly applied a 3-month horizon scaling (×√3) on top of the 3-month volatility. The expected formula appears to be reserves × Z × σ_3m / 100 (no additional √3 horizon scaling), since the 3-month volatility is already a 3-month measure. This Step 2 error cascades into Step 3 RaR values being ~√3× too high. The xlsx skill is a generic spreadsheet formatting guide and does not provide domain guidance on gold reserves-at-risk (RaR) calculation methodology, so it needs a task-specific clarification regarding the valuation exposure formula convention (do NOT multiply by √3 when σ is already a 3-month volatility).

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The xlsx skill covers general spreadsheet formatting/formula hygiene but does not contain domain procedure for computing gold reserves 'Gold valuation exposure (95% one-sided shock)'. The agent misinterpreted the exposure formula by scaling the already-3-month volatility by √3 (treating σ_3m as a monthly vol and annualizing to 3 months). Expected formula is: Exposure = Reserves × 1.645 × σ_3m / 100 (where σ_3m is the standard deviation of monthly log-returns×100 over the last 3 months, used directly as the shock magnitude). This caused all Step 2 risk cells and all Step 3 RaR% to be ~√3 (≈1.732) times too large.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a domain-procedure appendix (or a sibling note referenced from xlsx/SKILL.md) for reserves-at-risk / valuation-exposure calculations clarifying: (1) When a volatility labeled 'N-month volatility' is computed as STDEV of the last N monthly log-returns (×100), it already represents an N-month-horizon shock measure in percent and must NOT be further multiplied by √N when forming a one-sided VaR-style shock. (2) The 95% one-sided gold valuation exposure formula is: Exposure = GoldReserves × 1.645 × σ_3m / 100 (do not include an extra √3 term). (3) RaR% = Exposure / TotalReserves × 100. (4) For Step 2, countries in the Volume sheet with 2025 data but not in the Value sheet should be converted using the Jan–Sep 2025 average gold price. (5) For Step 3, drop any country lacking 2025 Total Reserves data before computing RaR. Explicitly warn against double-annualizing a horizon-matched volatility.
